title: mmap /dev/fb0
subtitle: A process paints the screen — Doom-class, not a blit toy
what_you_see: Pixels on the framebuffer. Doom, TinyX, or a probe that fills /dev/fb0 after mmap.
why_it_matters: Userspace does not talk to the GPU through a private IR0 API. It opens /dev/fb0, mmap MAP_SHARED, and writes pixels. The kernel maps the physical framebuffer into that process.

dual_view.kernel:
dev_fb0_open
  ↓ sys_mmap device_id 15
  ↓ map fb_phys into the process

steps.label: open /dev/fb0
steps.what_ir0_does: A real fd_table slot (devfs, device_id 15). Same node TinyX and Doom use.
steps.why_it_matters: No IR0-specific graphics ioctl required to get a mapping.

steps.label: mmap MAP_SHARED
steps.what_ir0_does: sys_mmap sees the fb0 fd and maps fb_phys pages into the process VA. Offset 0 is the start of the framebuffer.
steps.why_it_matters: Wrong fd or a dead VBE backend returns ENODEV/EBADF — honest errors, not a fake map.

steps.label: Writes become pixels
steps.what_ir0_does: Stores through the mapping hit the linear framebuffer. The probe (FASE58C) or DoomGeneric blits without a compositor.
steps.why_it_matters: T2 proof: a fullscreen client, not a kernel-side sprite.
